lesson_title: Your Body Is a Taxi Rank: Seven Jobs, One Machine
hook_text: When you sprint for a taxi, five body systems change in five seconds. Here is who does what.
clip_script: Your body is a taxi rank, and seven jobs keep it running. The food stall is the digestive system: vetkoek in, glucose out into the blood. The petrol pump is the respiratory system: oxygen in, carbon dioxide out. The taxis are the circulatory system: the heart is the engine, the blood is the fleet, delivering glucose and oxygen to every cell and hauling the rubbish back. The marshal with the whistle is the nervous system, in charge of everyone. Drivers and steel frames: the musculoskeletal system, bones and muscles. The cleaners: the excretory system, kidneys filtering urea out as urine. And the reproductive system plans the next generation. Now sprint. The marshal sees the taxi and fires your legs. In seconds your heart goes from 70 beats a minute to 150 and your breathing from 15 to 40, because the muscles want more glucose and oxygen. You sweat to stay at 37 degrees. One system changed because another needed it. Break one, and the rest suffer: asthma starves the muscles of oxygen even though the legs are fine. Nobody at the rank works alone.
visual_style: A bustling cartoon taxi rank where each stall lights up with its system's name; a sprinting figure makes the heart-rate and breathing counters spin up; one stall darkens and the others flicker.
pacing: Seven rapid stall beats, a sprint that accelerates the counters, a hard stop on the strike.
